# What Else Are They In — the gap against the source

> ⚠️ **Status: In Review — awaiting Human Operator approval. No code may be written until Status = Approved** (Constitution Art. II).
> 
> Split out of *Head to Head*, which raised it and then said — correctly — that it should be its own spec. That one PRODUCES a preference signal; this one CONSUMES it, and has its own decisions.
## Intention
Raised by the Human Operator: *"you really liked this actor — let's query the source and see what else they're in that you don't have."*
🚨 **This is a different KIND of feature from everything else in this project.** Every tool so far describes, corrects or connects what the library already contains. This one reports on things that are **not there** — the first time the app looks outward.
## Why it is possible now and was not last week
The hard part was never asking the source what a performer appears in. It is answering **"do I already have this?"**
| Before match edges | Now |
| --- | --- |
| Fuzzy title comparison — a guess, wrong often enough to be useless | ⭐ An **exact lookup**: does any `video_match` row carry this scene's source id? |
⭐ `ActorMetadataProvider.knownWorks(actorId:limit:)` already exists — built for the disambiguation picker — and already returns a performer's scenes. Since `98f0618` each candidate also carries `studioName` structured. **The diff against ****`video_match`**** is the only genuinely new logic.**
## 📊 The measurement this spec turns on
Measured against the drive library on 2026-08-09, after the matching campaign:
|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Actors carrying an identity | **1,341 / 1,353 — 99%** |
| Videos carrying an identity | 1,378 / 2,077 — 66% |
| Actor→video pairs identified | 3,138 / 3,771 — 83% |
The actor side is essentially finished, which is what makes the *query* possible. The video side is what decides whether the *answer* is trustworthy, and it is not uniform:
| Actors, by how much of their filmography is identified | Count | What a gap list would be |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **All** their videos identified | 971 (72%) | ⭐ Exact |
| **Some** identified | 218 (16%) | ⚠️ Over-reports |
| **None** identified | 163 (12%) | 🚨 Useless |
### 🚨 And it is worst for exactly the actors this feature is for
Among actors with **five or more videos** — the population a top tier is drawn from — only **72 of 172 (42%)** have every video identified.
That is not a surprise once stated: more videos means more chances that one was never matched. But it inverts the naive reading of "83% identified", and it means **the majority of the actors worth asking about would over-report**.
## 🔴 D1 — Per-actor confidence, not a blanket caveat
**This is the decision the feature turns on, and it is the one thing that makes it shippable now.**
The obvious response to the table above is a warning on the screen: *"some results may already be in your library"*. ⚠️ That is useless. A caveat that applies to everything tells the operator nothing about anything, and they will either ignore it or distrust the whole list.
⭐ **The over-report is measurable per actor, locally, at query time.** The app knows how many of that performer's videos lack an identity. So instead of a global disclaimer it can say something precise:
> **12 scenes you do not have.** 3 of your 9 videos with her are not identified, so up to 3 of these may already be on disk.
🔴 And when the count is zero, it should say so with equal precision — *"all 9 of your videos with her are identified, so this list is exact"*. A feature that is exactly right 72% of the time and says which 72% is far more useful than one that hedges uniformly.
## D2 — Ask only about contenders the operator ranked highly
⚠️ A sweep across 1,341 identified performers is a rate-limit problem and answers a question nobody asked. The top tier is a few dozen requests and answers the question they did.
⭐ This is a second, independent argument for *Head to Head*'s "build for the top tier first" — it is the only part of the ranking this feature needs.
✅ **Decision — BOTH.** The profile button for curiosity, the sweep for a worklist.
## 🔴 D3 — It produces a list, and nothing more
The app says *"these exist and you do not have them"* and stops. No fetching, no acquiring, no links followed automatically — consistent with the no-background-network posture and with the write path being out of scope. ✅ Already agreed by the Human Operator in the *Head to Head* spec.
⚠️ Corollary worth stating: this means the feature's output is **read and then acted on elsewhere, by hand**. If that turns out to be tedious, the answer is a better list — sortable, exportable — not an acquisition path.
## D4 — What counts as "I already have this"
An exact match on the source's own scene id, via `video_match(video_id, source, source_id)`.
⚠️ **Scoped to the SAME source.** A scene id from one provider means nothing to another, and comparing them would produce false "missing" entries that look like real ones. The query is per-source and the UI must not merge two sources' answers into one list.
⚠️ **A video the operator deleted deliberately will reappear** in every gap list forever. There is no record of "I had this and did not want it".
✅ **Decision — DEFERRED.** Not on day one. Revisit once the list has been used in anger; the operator may simply not care, and a dismiss list built before that would be guessing at what wants dismissing.
## D5 — Where the network cost lands
One `knownWorks` call per actor asked about, and the provider caps results with `limit`.
⚠️ `limit` is a real constraint, not a detail. A prolific performer's filmography can exceed any sane page size, and a truncated source list would silently under-report — the opposite failure from D1's, and much harder to notice because a short list looks like good news. **The UI must distinguish "nothing else found" from "showing the first N".**
✅ **Decision — a sequential sweep of roughly fifty.** Cancellable, with progress, never on a background schedule.
🔴 **And RANDOMISE the fifty until the ranking has real brackets.** The Human Operator's addition, and it closes a hole in this spec.
⚠️ W7 says not to sweep a provisional contender, because the ranking has not earned the right to name a top tier. Taken alone that would block the feature entirely right now: after 38 comparisons nearly every contender is under the threshold, so "the top fifty" does not yet exist and a strict reading returns nobody.
⭐ So the selection has two modes and the app picks between them by looking at the data:
| When | Sweep |
| --- | --- |
| Enough settled contenders to form a top tier | The top fifty by score |
| Not yet | **Fifty at random** from actors that carry an identity |
Random is not a placeholder — it is the correct answer while the ladder is young. Every actor is equally likely to be interesting, so an arbitrary fifty is exactly as informative as any other fifty and costs the same fifty requests. ⚠️ The UI must SAY which mode it used, or an early sweep will read as a ranked recommendation and be judged as one.
## Test strategy (Constitution Art. III)
- **W1** — A scene whose source id appears in `video_match` is NOT reported as missing.
- **W2** — A scene whose source id is absent IS reported as missing.
- **W3** — 🚨 A scene id from a DIFFERENT source is never treated as a match.
- **W4** — The confidence line counts the actor's unidentified videos correctly, for zero, some and all.
- **W5** — An actor with no identified videos is reported as such rather than being handed a list of everything the source knows.
- **W6** — A truncated source response is presented as truncated, not as a complete answer.
- **W7** — A provisional contender is not swept AS A TOP-TIER PICK. ⚠️ But a young ranking falls back to a random fifty rather than to nobody, and the two modes are distinguishable in the result.
- **W8** — Nothing in the feature writes to the library. Asserted directly: it is a read-only feature and should stay one.
## ❓ Open questions — Human Operator
1. **D2** — profile button, top-tier sweep, or both?
2. **D4** — is a "do not show me this again" list needed on day one?
3. **D5** — is a sequential fifty-request sweep acceptable, or should the first version be one actor at a time?
4. ✅ **Scope — ACTORS ONLY.** A studio's catalogue is far larger and the same over-report analysis has not been done for it.
